content.title: Trader Joe’s expands recall over glass contamination fears
content.text: John Tomase John Tomase Published Mar 24, 2026 Trader Joe's has expanded a recall of frozen meals to 43 states over concerns the food could contain glass, The Boston Globe reports. The Food and Drug Administration posted a recent notice warning that tainted meals, including some chicken and rice dinners, could include pieces of glass from 1 to 3 centimeters long. Ajinomoto Foods of Portland, Ore., issued its first recall of more than 3 million pounds on Feb. 19 and has since upped that total to 37 million pounds. Consumers should discard or return any affected items. Editors’ Picks Trader Joe's recalled 37 million pounds of frozen products for potential glass contamination. Affected items include Chicken Fried Rice, Vegetable Fried Rice and Chicken Shu Mai produced by Ajinomoto Foods. Glass contamination recalls affecting 37 million pounds signal systemic production failures, not isolated incidents. Your business needs to understand that Trader Joe's recalling this volume means the contamination source affected multiple production runs across extended timeframes. When best-by dates span February 2026 to August 2027, the glass entered products for over a year before detection. The recall originated from consumer complaints finding glass pieces in food. Trader Joe's and supplier Ajinomoto Foods didn't catch the contamination through quality control. Customers discovered it by nearly eating glass. -) 37 million pounds recalled -) Glass contamination across multiple products -) Best-by dates span 18 months -) Triggered by customer complaints, not internal testing No injuries reported yet doesn't mean the recall succeeded. It means people haven't been hurt badly enough to report it or haven't eaten the contaminated products yet. Glass in food is unacceptable quality failure regardless of injury count. Implement quality controls that catch contamination before customer complaints. Trace production issues immediately when any contamination is detected. Recognize that volume this large getting recalled means your safety systems failed for extended periods. Does your quality control catch contamination before it reaches customers, or do you wait for complaints before investigating production failures? Trader Joe's has expanded its recall of frozen products due to potential glass contamination, affecting approximately 37 million pounds of food. This recall includes popular items like Chicken Fried Rice, Vegetable Fried Rice, and Chicken Shu Mai, triggered by consumer complaints about glass pieces found in these products. The affected items were produced by Ajinomoto Foods North America and have best-by dates ranging from February 28, 2026, to August 19, 2027. Customers are advised to check their freezers and discard any recalled products or return them to the store for a full refund. While no injuries have been reported, this recall highlights the importance of vigilant food safety practices. Trader Joe's emphasizes its commitment to maintaining high safety standards and is working closely with the USDA to resolve the issue. Nearly 10 million more pounds of popular Trader Joe's frozen food items have been recalled amid an ongoing recall after multiple customer complaints about pieces of glass in the products, according to an FDA notice. The affected items, 16 of them, were distributed in more than two dozen states, including New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut. They were sold under brand names at Trader Joe's, Kroger, Ling Ling, and Tai Pei. Ajinomoto Foods North America, which manufactures the items, initiated the recall about five weeks ago, after receiving multiple complaints about glass found in the products. Trader Joe's frozen food recall expands: Watch out for glass in these products nbcnewyork.app.link Trader Joe's says it errs on the side of extreme caution and stores will remove items from shelves and issue refunds if there's any risk of danger. Still, the company's frequent recalls have grown common enough to consider that the surge in problems could mean Trader Joe's isn't sourcing its foods from farms or factories which prioritize safety measures to the degree it proclaims. In the most recent recall, Ajimoto Foods North America Inc. announced it is recalling nearly 10M pounds of Trader Joe’s Vegetable Fried Rice due to the presence of “foreign objects.” The notice stated that the foreign object was glass, measuring 1-3 cm long and 2-4 mm wide. The affected product was distributed in 43 states and have best buy dates between March 5, 2026, and Oct. 23, 2026. Regardless of how often it happens, stay up to date with the latest food recalls before you bite into anything. Food Recall Expands to Include Ramen, Dumplings, and Other Asian Foods From Trader Joe’s, Costco, and More - Real Simple realsimple.com Trader Joe’s puts its name on almost everything it sells. While store brands, known as private labels, used to suggest poor quality, Trader Joe’s has made them cool. It has built a cult following for its seasonal products and frozen section. But the chain keeps one big secret: who makes its products. Because the company is privately held, it’s not required to disclose its suppliers. However, there is one loophole. When a product is recalled, the US Food and Drug Administration reveals what the issue is and who made the item. So we dug through dozens of FDA recall filings to piece together who’s hiding behind Trader Joe’s famous private label. Watch full video: https://lnkd.in/gMTiBfpB
